Odenkirk makes this crushing failure visceral: the initial desperation, the fleeting joy, the catastrophic fall—a performance of extraordinary architecture and energy that lifts the role to classic stature.
The ensemble cast is brilliant and bring authenticity and believability to each of their characters.
David Mamet's brackish masterpiece is in solid hands in Patrick Marber's production.
The acting could use a tweak here and there, it’s true, but, in general, this cast is doing what it was hired to do, from the top down, and few visitors will be disappointed.

Given the high prices the production is asking for tickets, the inconsistency of the acting, and the unwise choice of using a less-than-intimate theater, I feel those who spend their money on this “Glengarry Glen Ross” are getting an even rawer deal than the show’s characters.
